name: Authenticate a sender domain
intent: Trigger authentication checks for a sender domain (Brevo code, DKIM, DMARC).
description: Authenticates a specific domain. Use this to: - Authenticate a domain - Verify DNS record configuration - Complete domain setup for sending - Enable domain for email authentication Key information returned: - Authentication success confirmation - Domain readiness status for email sending
when_to_use: After DNS records are configured and before sending production traffic.
when_not_to_use: Do not use repeatedly without changing DNS — check the returned configuration first.
preconditions: Domain added to the account
DNS records configured

auth.notes: API key auth is the default for server-to-server use. OAuth 2.0 (including M2M) is available for apps acting on behalf of a user.

name: Create email sender
intent: Create a sender identity (from name/email) that campaigns and transactional emails can use.
description: Creates a new email sender in your Brevo account. **Use this to:** - Add new senders for email campaigns - Configure sender identity (name and email) - Associate dedicated IPs with the sender (for dedicated IP accounts) - Set up domain-based sender configurations **Key information returned:** - Created sender ID - DKIM and SPF configuration status - Success confirmation **Important considerations:** - Verification email sent to specified sender address - DKIM and SPF configuration affects deliverability - Dedicated IP accounts require IP association during creation - IP weights must sum to 10…
when_to_use: When a new brand, domain or team needs its own From address.
when_not_to_use: Do not use if the domain is not authenticated — deliverability will suffer.
preconditions: Access to the mailbox for OTP validation
Domain ideally authenticated
